chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, said,
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who marries his daughter to a drinker of the wine, so he has cut off his relationship'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a daughter to a wine drinker in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that marrying one's daughter to a wine-drinker severs the familial bond (rahim), a ruling rooted in the Shia tradition where 'severing rahim' implies a spiritual and social disconnection rather than merely physical kinship. This highlights the juristic principle that a spouse's moral character, particularly regarding major sins like intoxication, directly impacts the integrity of the extended family unit. The emphasis on piety in marital selection underscores the broader Islamic value of preserving lineage and social stability through righteous unions.
